_comment: Golden truth for challenge_01.docx — Slice D (known-evil adversarial DOCX). Parser: pandoc (via pypandoc → HTML). Each challenge is described in challenge_descriptions. Sections marked with known_parser_limitations are EXPECTED failures in the current implementation.
_format_note: Top-level fields (footnotes, headings, tables, …) describe the IDEAL target output a fully-correct parser should produce. They are NOT a snapshot of what the current parser produces. current_parser_output documents what pandoc actually produces today. Tests that assert the ideal target and currently fail are marked @pytest.mark.xfail.

pandoc.description:
OOXML footnotes are converted by pandoc to
  1. ...
. The HTML parser's detect_html_footnotes() only handles

style — the pandoc output format is not handled. Result: 0 Footnote elements produced; footnote text silently dropped; inline anchors remain as raw HTML inside body Paragraph elements.

python-docx creates separate numbering definitions for List Bullet / List Bullet 2 / List Bullet 3 paragraph styles. Pandoc converts these to separate <ul> blocks rather than a single nested <ul>. The HTML parser then produces one DocumentList per <ul>, yielding 5 separate bullet lists and 4 separate numbered lists instead of 1 nested bullet list and 1 nested numbered list.

Long heading text is wrapped by pandoc at ~80 chars, injecting \r\n inside the heading HTML. BeautifulSoup preserves this whitespace when computing Heading.text. Result: 'Tables: Truth Versus\r\nDecoration' instead of 'Tables: Truth Versus Decoration'.

heading_gap.summary: A Heading 3 ('Genuine Subsection') appears directly under a Heading 1 ('Headings and Their Impostors') with no Heading 2 in between. Parsers must NOT invent an intermediate H2.

fake_list.summary: Four plain paragraphs are manually typed as '1.', '2.', '3.', 'a.' — no OOXML list numbering (<w:numPr>) applied. An ideal parser applying normalization would promote them to a DocumentList; a basic parser leaves them as Paragraphs.

chaos_paragraph.summary: ONE Word paragraph containing four logical sentences joined by w:br manual line breaks. Visually renders as four separate lines but is structurally a single paragraph.

Chaos line two: Attendance was recorded by the duty secretary.
Chaos line three: The minutes of the previous meeting were adopted without amendment.
Chaos line four: The session was adjourned sine die at 10:45.
